The main takeaway from our work is that
the combinatorial complexity of a denable set in an o-mininal structure is controlled by the combinatorial structure of the underlying structure.
the combinatorial structure of sets in o-minimal structures is governed by the same principles as in semi-algebraic or semi-Pfaff sets.

the combinatorial complexity of a denable set is determined by the complexity of a dening formula, rather than the description complexity of the dened sets themselves, and this complexity is controlled by a single combinatorial invariant, the so-called Betti numbers.
